entries.description: Register.

**Write the missing Set 125 changelog fragment, then fold both targets.** Author `ai_router/changelog.d/` fragment for the read-only tool grant: what a routed call could do before (arbitrary shell, file create/edit, sub-agent spawning against the live working tree), what it can do now (`view`, `grep`, `glob`), and why it matters (a verifier able to edit the code it judges can report VERIFIED on its own edit). State it as the consumer-visible security-relevant change it is, not as a refactor. Then run `python -m ai_router.changelog fold --target router` and `--target extension` so the tagged commit carries real version sections rather than 16 loose fragments. **Do not invent entries for sets that already have fragments** — fold what is there; the gap being closed is Set 125 specifically. **Then make the breaking change self-remedying in the same pass.** The `1.0.0` section must state, at the top and in one screen: the symptom a user actually sees (config load refuses the spec), the one-line fix, and a working link to `docs/cross-repo-lightweight-removal-notice.md`. This replaces detection with remediation on purpose — it reaches every consumer of an open-source package, which no sweep of known checkouts can do.

**Rework the extension README into the Marketplace listing.** This is the pitch, and it is the artifact six staff and every future adopter read. Lead with what the framework *is* — the work is organized and standardized, and the verification is one you can check — not with what the AI writes. Use the new `media/ai-work-explorer.png` (committed in `d370e8f0`), referenced by **absolute raw.githubusercontent URL** like the existing image; a relative path does not render on the Marketplace. Also refresh `package.json`'s `description` and `keywords`, which are what Marketplace *search results* show and which are equally baked at publish. **Claim auditability, never efficacy.** Supported: the verifier is chosen by excluding the orchestrator's own provider (resolved from the model id, not a self-reported label); a session blocks rather than passing when no different-provider verifier exists; a close with no cross-provider evidence runs the verification itself; a finding closes only when its criterion fails before the fix and passes after; rounds are bounded and only the operator may authorize another; full suites run before commit, push and close. **Not supported and not to be claimed:** any defect-catch rate or "catches bugs before they ship" — the framework has never measured what fraction of real defects it finds. Keep the register of the existing docs (*"it is containment, not a sandbox, and the docs must not claim otherwise"*); that candour is the most credible asset here and a marketing pass must not sand it off.

**Correct the root README's two false statements.** It calls the tree "Session Set Explorer" (Set 132 S1 renamed it to **AI Work Explorer**, and `package.json` agrees; the stale phrase is line-wrapped, so grep for both halves). And its Prerequisites section states API-key accounts for all three providers are required — wrong for the Copilot-seat population that Sets 078/112 exist to serve, and wrong for the six staff now using it. Reconcile it with the seat path described earlier in the same file.

Wrote the Set 125 read-only tool grant fragment (Security), folded 17 router + 13 extension fragments, restructured both pending regions into the [1.0.0] / [0.51.0] version sections being tagged, and made the breaking change self-remedying at the top of 1.0.0 (symptom, one-line diff, working notice link). Restamped both baselines; round trip OK.

Reworked the extension README as the Marketplace listing: leads with what the framework is and that the verification is checkable, hero image swapped to media/ai-work-explorer.png by absolute raw.githubusercontent URL with descriptive alt text, added a 'Verification you can check' section carrying only the six supported auditability claims plus an explicit 'what this does not claim' block (no defect-catch rate) and the containment-not-a-sandbox register. Removed two false statements: the $0-budget 'or you skip verification' bullet (no skip exists post-1.0.0) and 'all three API keys are required'. Re-framed the 73/32% savings as the hypothetical Opus-baseline counterfactual the report actually computes. Refreshed package.json description + keywords.

Corrected both false statements in the root README: the activity-bar view is AI Work Explorer (Set 132 S1 rename, package.json agrees), and Prerequisites no longer requires API-key accounts for all three providers -- it now states the two answers (DIRECT_API with two of three keys as the working minimum, or a keyless COPILOT_CLI seat) and points at verify_type, reconciling with the seat path described earlier in the same file. RESIDUAL, out of scope by the spec's Non-goals: 'Session Set Explorer' survives in 25 other markdown files (most are dated proposals; the live ones are close-out.md, copilot-seat-setup-checklist.md, repository-reference.md, session-state-schema.md, spec-md-schema.md).

4 rounds, gpt-5-6-sol throughout, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider via model-registry lookup. R1 discovery (2-way fan-out, spec-conformance + failure-scenario lenses): 1 Major -- the listing promised an unconditional cross-provider block while the same release documents an accepted same-provider fallback. R2 supplementary (harvest before remediating, per loop discipline): VERIFIED, 0 new. R3 remediation-review: REJECTED the fix -- package.json had been re-worded ('independent verification built into every close') rather than fixed, and the changelog argued the point instead of reporting it. R4 remediation-review: VERIFIED, fix accepted, 0 findings. Both rejections were correct and are recorded in the round-1 and round-3 remediation sidecars. Routed cost $2.5455.

All three declared suites run fresh and green against the final tree: pytest 4664 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (205.8s, -n 8 per the operator cap, route journaled), mocha 1458 passing (23s), playwright 32 passed (2.9m). run_of_record affected named all three because package.json sits in mocha's and playwright's covers and the changelogs sit in pytest's. pytest and mocha were re-taken after Layer 3, which rebuilds dist/ inside both suites' covers. Layer 3's earlier 32/32 failure was a stuck VS Code installer holding the vscode-updating mutex, resolved by the operator applying the pending update; nothing was changed to make it pass.
Register.

**Confirm both registries are live and correct the release-status row.** Verify `dabbler-ai-router 1.0.0` on PyPI and the extension `0.51.0` on the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX, then update `docs/repository-reference.md` → *Current release status* to say what is live rather than what is staged. **This row has been wrong twice** — Set 112 S3 found it still naming `0.33.0` live nine releases on, and Set 107 S1 found it claiming `0.46.0` was staged after it had shipped. Both times the publish happened and the row was never updated, which is why correcting it is a named deliverable and not bookkeeping. Record the workflow run ids and the tagged commit, as the surrounding rows do.

**Journal the deletion-cost ruling.** Operator decision, `authority=human`, via `python -m ai_router.decision_journal`: *deleting a test whose only subject is deleted code is not a verification reduction.* The reasoning to record: the framework currently makes addition cheap and deletion expensive, because deleting a module means deleting its tests, and reducing verification is a hard human-only carve-out that an orchestrator may never self-authorize. Measured symptoms — 4,640 tests, ~+29 test functions/day, **zero guards ever retired**; Set 116 S3 demoted five gates and deliberately deleted nothing; of six modules scheduled for deletion three went and the three survivors *grew* (`contract_gate` 1,158 → 1,319, `spec_admission` 403 → 1,082, `replacement_gate` 546 → 652). Pair it with the extension of the existing rule *"no gate is added without deleting one"* from gates to **modules**. This is a ruling, not an implementation: no code changes here.

Rewrote both release-status rows to say what is live, added the coordinated-release walk entry, and corrected two false historical claims found in the same pass (the 0.45.0 row claimed an Open VSX publish that its own run log shows was skipped; the 0.32.0 walk bullet still said 'not yet on PyPI').

Journaled the operator's deletion-cost ruling: a test whose only subject is deleted code falls OUTSIDE the verification carve-out, paired with extending 'no gate is added without deleting one' from gates to modules, and gated on a subject-is-gone precondition. authority=human, rubric_line=value-trade-off, verification_effect=none, operator_attestation cites the spec. The three module line counts were re-derived (1319/1082/652) rather than inherited. No code changed.

Six rounds. Rounds 1-4 ran on gemini-pro (tier 2) because every OpenAI model returned 429 all session; the escalation ladder's rung 2, journaled, with the tier degradation stated not buried. Five Majors from the two discovery passes plus two on the fix delta: three false positives settled by deterministic evidence, two accepted and fixed. The operator then restored OpenAI credit and authorized round 5 on gpt-5-6-sol -- a genuine third provider -- which accepted all six surviving fix verdicts, closing the disputed finding by independent acceptance rather than by adjudication of my argument, and caught one real new defect of mine (four hand-authored decision timestamps, one of them chronologically impossible). Corrected and disclosed. Round 6, on a second separate authorization, returned VERIFIED with zero findings and all nine ledger entries accepted.

All three declared suites green and fresh against the final tree. pytest 4656 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed in 223s at -n 8 (re-run after the decisions.jsonl correction staled the first green run); the single xfail is the deliberate strict-xfail pinning Session 1's open changelog.check() gap. mocha 1468 passing / 0 failing in 23s. playwright 32 passed / 0 failed in 3.1m. mocha and playwright were not re-run for the journal correction and are not owed -- decisions.jsonl sits under docs/session-sets/, which run_of_record affected confirms is covered by pytest alone.

Closed VERIFIED. close_session passed every gate (checklist_posted WARN, advisory, disclosed not backfilled) and REFUSED the cost block as malformed -- corrected afterwards to Session 1's shape and re-validated clean against _validate_cost, with the gap disclosed since the closeout event cannot carry the figure retroactively. Notification fired after the close succeeded. Step 9 recorded in change-log.md: NO preload changes, on a corpus sitting at exactly 100% of every ceiling; the three durable learnings routed to an executable fix, to the release-status row, and to Set 134 respectively.
